page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is a storage-dense instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. The host hardware utilizes an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz across 6 physical cores and 12 virtual CPUs with hyperthreading. It is configured with 48.0 GB of RAM, yielding 4.0 GB per vCPU. The server bundles a high-capacity local storage subsystem consisting of 35,433 GB (approximately 35.4 TB) on mechanical hard disk drives (HDD). Network connectivity is established with a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Synthetic benchmark evaluations indicate weak single-core performance, evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1102.49 and a Geekbench single-core score of 911.0. Multi-core compute performance sits in the middle 50% relative tier, recording 8789.97 on stress-ng multi-core and 4584.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Memory read bandwidth reaches 54.9 GB/sec for large uncached blocks and 488.85 GB/sec for small cached blocks, while write bandwidth measures 47.08 GB/sec. Under database simulation benchmarks, the server completes 8.27 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 3193.71 on PassMark database operations.

The ecs.d1.3xlarge provides high qualitative storage density per vCPU, sacrificing I/O latency by leveraging mechanical HDDs rather than solid-state NVMe drives. While single-threaded processing and static web serving throughput are constrained, the instance offers balanced multi-core execution for memory and capacity-bound workloads. It is suited for log processing, big data batch analytics, data archiving, ETL pipelines, and secondary database storage.
description: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is a storage-dense virtual instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. It provides 12 vCPUs across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, 48.0 GB of RAM, and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. A defining feature is its integrated 35,433 GB local HDD storage capacity. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate weak single-thread performance (Geekbench single-core score 911.0), balanced by average multi-threaded throughput (PassMark CPU score 10074.03) and 8.27 million Redis SET operations per second. The presence of dense local HDD capacity makes this instance cost-effective for large-scale data retention, batch processing, and big data workloads requiring extensive disk capacity without requiring high-cost NVMe drives.
